description: State Machine Builder page -- design and manage state machine configs with states, transitions, graph visualization, pathfinding, discovery exploration, live testing, and import/export. Users select or create configs from a header dropdown, then work across seven tabs: Graph (visual node-edge layout via dagre), States (list + spatial view), Transitions (list with action playback), Pathfinding (find optimal paths between states), Discovery (automated state exploration with strategies), Live Test (manual transition execution and navigation), and Export/Import (JSON file operations).

groups.name: Page Header and Config Selector
groups.description: The page header shows a GitBranch icon, the title 'State Machine', and a config selector dropdown. Users pick an existing config to load it, or click 'New' to create one. A trash icon deletes the active config with a confirmation dialog. A loading spinner appears during async operations.

assertions.description: The page displays a clear 'State Machine' title in the header so users know they are on the state machine builder
Users see a config selector dropdown with a 'Select config...' placeholder option to choose which state machine config to work with
Users can click the 'New' button to begin creating a new state machine config
When a config is active, a trash icon button allows users to delete it after confirmation
preconditions: An active config must be selected

groups.name: Empty State (No Config Selected)
groups.description: When no config is selected, the page shows a centered empty state with a GitBranch icon and instructional text prompting the user to select or create a config.

assertions.description: When no config is selected, users see instructional text guiding them to select or create a config

criteria.textContent: Select a config or create a new one to get started.

assertions.description: Even in the empty state, the config selector dropdown is present so users can select an existing config
When no config is selected, the tab bar should not be visible since there is no config data to work with

target.label: Tab bar absent in empty state

groups.name: Create Config Flow
groups.description: Clicking 'New' reveals an inline input with a text field for the config name, a 'Create' button, and a 'Cancel' button. Users type a name and press Enter or click Create to persist the config via the sm_create_config IPC command.

assertions.description: The new config input field shows a 'Config name...' placeholder to indicate what to type
A 'Create' button submits the new config name to the backend
A 'Cancel' button dismisses the new config input without creating anything
The Create button is disabled when the name input is empty, preventing submission of blank config names
assertions.expected: The Create button should be visually disabled (opacity-50) when the name field is empty or whitespace-only

groups.name: Tab Navigation Bar
groups.description: Seven tabs appear below the header when a config is active: Graph, States, Transitions, Pathfinding, Discovery, Live Test, and Export / Import. The active tab is highlighted with a brand-primary bottom border. Each tab has an icon and label.

assertions.description: The Graph tab provides access to the interactive dagre-based node-edge visualization of states and transitions
The States tab shows a tabular view of all states in the config with selection support
The Transitions tab lists all transitions between states with selection and editing support
The Pathfinding tab enables users to find optimal paths between states in the config graph
The Discovery tab provides automated state exploration with configurable strategies
The Live Test tab provides manual controls to execute transitions and navigate to states
The Export / Import tab provides JSON file export and import operations for state machine configs
Exactly 7 tabs are rendered in the tab bar when a config is active
assertions.expected: The tab bar section below the header should contain exactly 7 tab buttons: Graph, States, Transitions, Pathfinding, Discovery, Live Test, Export / Import

groups.name: Graph Tab Content
groups.description: The Graph tab renders an interactive node-edge graph using @xyflow/react with dagre layout. States are nodes and transitions are edges. Floating action buttons allow adding new states and transitions. Clicking a node selects that state; clicking an edge selects the transition. An empty graph shows an instructional message.

assertions.description: A floating 'Add State' button on the graph tab allows users to create a new state, opening the new-state form in the sidebar
A floating 'Add Transition' button on the graph tab allows users to create a new transition between states
When no states exist, the graph shows an instructional empty message guiding users to import or use Discovery
assertions.expected: No states in this config
preconditions: A config is selected with zero states

assertions.description: Clicking a state node in the graph selects it and opens the state detail sidebar, deselecting any previously selected transition
assertions.expected: Clicking a state node should: (1) highlight the node with brand-primary ring, (2) open the right sidebar showing 'State Detail' header, (3) deselect any previously selected transition
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one state

groups.name: Graph Visualization Controls
groups.description: The graph canvas has control buttons in the top-right (Fit, keyboard shortcut toggle, Re-layout), a stats panel in the bottom-left (state count, transition count, initial state), a MiniMap, and keyboard shortcuts. Nodes display element grids, badges (START, outgoing/incoming counts), and confidence indicators.

assertions.description: A 'Fit' button in the graph controls panel adjusts the viewport to show all nodes
assertions.expected: The graph canvas should have a 'Fit' button (with Maximize icon) in the top-right controls panel that fits all nodes into view when clicked
preconditions: A config is selected with states

assertions.description: A 'Re-layout' button in the graph controls re-runs the dagre automatic layout algorithm
assertions.expected: The graph controls panel should include a Re-layout button (with LayoutGrid icon) that recalculates node positions using dagre layout
preconditions: A config is selected with states

assertions.description: A '?' button toggles a keyboard shortcuts overlay showing Escape (deselect), F (fit), L (re-layout), Tab (cycle states), I (jump to initial), Delete (delete transition), and +/- (zoom)
assertions.expected: After clicking the '?' button, a 'Keyboard Shortcuts' overlay should appear listing all available shortcuts: Esc, ?, F, L, +/-, Tab, I, and Delete

assertions.description: State nodes in the graph display contextual badges: 'START' for initial states, outgoing transition count (top-right), incoming transition count (bottom-right), and a 'no links' badge for disconnected states
assertions.expected: State nodes should show a gold 'START' badge on initial states, an outgoing count badge (top-right), an incoming count badge (bottom-right), and a 'no links' badge on disconnected states. Each node also shows element count and confidence percentage.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

assertions.description: Transition edges display inline labels with the transition name, action type icons, action count, and path cost when not 1.0
assertions.expected: Each transition edge should render a pill-shaped label showing: action type icons (first 3 unique types, color-coded), transition name (truncated), path cost (if != 1.0), action count badge (if > 1), and a green Eye icon if the transition stays visible
preconditions: A config is selected with transitions

groups.name: States Tab Content
groups.description: The States tab shows all states using the shared StateViewPanel component with a 2-pane layout: left sidebar (state list with search/filter and view toggle) and right detail panel. It supports List and Spatial view modes. An 'Add State' button floats in the top-right corner.

assertions.description: The States tab has its own 'Add State' button in the top-right corner for creating new states while viewing the state list

target.label: Add State button on states tab

assertions.description: The states panel shows a 'States' heading with a count badge showing the total number of states
A search input with 'Filter states...' placeholder allows users to filter the state list by name
A List/Spatial view mode toggle allows switching between a text list view and a force-directed spatial canvas view of states
assertions.expected: The states panel should have two toggle buttons (List and Spatial/BarChart3 icons) that switch between a collapsible text list and a force-directed canvas view of state nodes

assertions.description: Clicking a state in the states tab selects it and opens the state detail sidebar for editing
assertions.expected: Clicking a state row should select the state, open the right sidebar with 'State Detail' header, and allow editing the state's properties
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one state

assertions.description: When no state is selected, the detail area shows 'Select a state to view its details' placeholder message
assertions.expected: The right pane of the states tab should show instructional text like 'Select a state to view its details' when no state is selected

groups.name: Transitions Tab Content
groups.description: The Transitions tab shows all transitions using the shared TransitionsPanel component with a left sidebar (searchable transition list with state filters) and a right detail panel with action playback controls. An 'Add Transition' button floats in the top-right corner.

assertions.description: The Transitions tab has its own 'Add Transition' button in the top-right corner for creating new transitions

target.label: Add Transition button on transitions tab

assertions.description: The transitions panel shows a 'Transitions' heading with a count badge showing the total number of transitions
A search input with 'Search transitions...' placeholder allows users to filter the transition list
Two state filter dropdowns ('All from states' and 'All target states') allow filtering transitions by source and destination states
assertions.expected: The transitions panel should have two dropdown filters: 'All from states' and 'All target states' that filter the transition list by source and destination states respectively

assertions.description: When a transition is selected, the detail panel shows 'Action Playback' controls with play/pause, step forward/back, reset, speed selector, progress bar, and timeline dots
assertions.expected: Selecting a transition should reveal an 'Action Playback' section with: speed dropdown (0.5x-4x), progress bar, control buttons (Reset, Step Back, Play/Pause, Step Forward), timeline dots for each action, and 'Action X of N' progress text
preconditions: A config is selected with transitions

assertions.description: Clicking a transition in the list selects it and opens the transition detail panel with action playback
assertions.expected: Clicking a transition row should select the transition, show its name and metadata in the detail panel, and enable action playback controls
preconditions: A config is selected with at least one transition

groups.name: Pathfinding Tab Content
groups.description: The Pathfinding tab provides graph pathfinding between states. Users select a 'From' and 'To' state from dropdowns, choose an algorithm (Dijkstra or BFS), and click 'Find Path'. Results show the path steps with transition names and costs, or a 'No path found' error. A 'Clear' button resets the results.

assertions.description: The pathfinding panel shows a 'Pathfinding' heading
A 'From' dropdown allows users to select the starting state for pathfinding with a 'Select state...' placeholder
A 'To' dropdown allows users to select the destination state for pathfinding with a 'Select state...' placeholder
A 'Find Path' button triggers the pathfinding algorithm between the selected from and to states
An algorithm dropdown allows choosing between Dijkstra (cheapest path) and BFS (shortest path) algorithms
assertions.expected: A dropdown should offer at least two pathfinding algorithms: 'Dijkstra (cheapest)' and 'BFS (shortest)', defaulting to Dijkstra

assertions.description: After finding a path, results show 'Path found (X steps)' with total cost, and a list of steps with transition name, cost, from/to states. If same state, shows 'Already at target state'. If no path, shows 'No path found'.
assertions.expected: After clicking 'Find Path': (1) Success: 'Path found (X step(s))' in green with 'Total cost: N.N', step list showing transition name and from→to states. (2) Same state: 'Already at target state'. (3) No path: 'No path found between specified states' in red.
preconditions: A config is selected with states

groups.name: Sidebar: New State Form
groups.description: When 'Add State' is clicked, a right sidebar (w-80) opens with a 'New State' header, a Name input, a Description textarea, and a 'Create State' submit button. The sidebar has a close (X) button. The name field has placeholder 'e.g., Login Page' and description has 'Optional description'. Enter key in the name field submits if non-empty. The button is disabled when the name is empty or creation is in progress.

assertions.description: The sidebar shows a 'NEW STATE' header label so users know they are creating a new state
Users see a Name input field with placeholder 'e.g., Login Page' for entering the new state's name
Users see a Description textarea with placeholder 'Optional description' for entering a description of the state
A 'Create State' button submits the new state to the backend via the sm_create_state IPC command
The sidebar has a close button (X icon) with aria-label 'Close sidebar' to dismiss the sidebar panel
A 'Name' label identifies the state name input field

groups.name: Sidebar: State Detail Panel
groups.description: When a state is selected, the sidebar shows a 'State Detail' header and renders the shared StateDetailPanel component with editable name, description, metadata grid (state ID, confidence, element count, render count), element list with type-colored badges, acceptance criteria list, domain knowledge cards, and save/delete actions.

assertions.description: The sidebar shows a 'STATE DETAIL' header label when an existing state is selected for editing
The state detail panel shows an editable Name input field pre-filled with the selected state's name
assertions.expected: An editable Name text input should be pre-filled with the current state's name, allowing the user to rename the state

assertions.description: The state detail panel displays a 2x2 metadata grid showing State ID, Confidence percentage, Elements count, and Renders count
assertions.expected: A metadata grid should display: State ID (monospace), Confidence (color-coded: green >= 80%, amber 50-79%, red < 50%), Elements count, and Renders count

assertions.description: The state detail panel shows an Elements list with type-colored badges (testid: blue, role: green, text: amber, ui: purple, url/nav: cyan) and the ability to add/remove elements
assertions.expected: An Elements section should list each element with a type-colored badge. Users can remove elements (x button) and add new elements using a 'type:element-id' input with an Add button.
preconditions: A state is selected with elements

assertions.description: The state detail panel provides 'Save Changes' and 'Delete State' buttons for persisting edits or removing the state
assertions.expected: A 'Save Changes' button (brand-primary, shown only when changes exist) persists edits via sm_update_state. A 'Delete State' button (red border) removes the state via sm_delete_state.

groups.name: Sidebar: Transition Editor
groups.description: When a transition is selected, the sidebar shows a 'Transition Detail' header and renders the shared TransitionEditor component. When 'Add Transition' is clicked, the same TransitionEditor appears in create mode with a 'New Transition' header. The editor provides state toggle groups (From, Activate, Exit), name input, action list with type-specific fields, path cost, and stays-visible checkbox.

assertions.description: The sidebar shows a 'NEW TRANSITION' header label when creating a new transition
The sidebar shows a 'TRANSITION DETAIL' header label when an existing transition is selected
The transition editor shows three state toggle groups: 'From States' (blue), 'Activate States' (green), and 'Exit States' (red), each rendering toggleable buttons for available states
assertions.expected: Three labeled toggle groups should be visible: 'From States' (blue accent), 'Activate States' (green accent), and 'Exit States' (red accent). Each group shows state names as toggleable buttons that highlight when selected.
preconditions: Transition editor is open (new or existing)

assertions.description: The transition editor has an Actions section with '+ Add Action' button and action fields with type dropdown (click, type, navigate, wait, etc.) and type-specific parameter fields
assertions.expected: An 'Actions' section should show: '+ Add Action' button, and for each action: a type dropdown (click, doubleClick, type, navigate, wait, select, scroll, drag, etc.) with conditional fields (target element ID for click actions, text field for type actions, URL for navigate, delay for wait, etc.)

assertions.description: The transition editor has 'Path Cost' number input and 'Stays Visible' checkbox options
assertions.expected: A 'Path Cost' number input (min 0, step 0.1) and a 'Stays Visible' checkbox should be present at the bottom of the transition editor

assertions.description: The transition editor has a 'Create' button (new mode) or 'Update' button (edit mode) and a 'Delete' button (edit mode only)
assertions.expected: In create mode: a 'Create' button (brand-primary). In edit mode: an 'Update' button (brand-primary) and a 'Delete' button (red border). The Create/Update button is disabled when the transition name is empty.

groups.name: Export / Import Tab
groups.description: The Export/Import tab provides buttons to export the current config to a JSON file and import a config from a JSON file. It shows the current config summary (name, state count, transition count). Import errors are displayed in a red error banner. Export uses Tauri's save dialog; import uses Tauri's open dialog.

assertions.description: The export tab shows an 'Export / Import' section heading
An 'Export Config' button saves the active config as a JSON file through Tauri's save dialog
An 'Import Config' button opens Tauri's file picker to select a JSON config file for import
The export tab displays a summary of the current config showing its name and counts of states and transitions
The config summary shows the number of states and transitions (e.g., '5 states, 8 transitions')
assertions.expected: states

groups.name: Discovery Tab: State Explorer Configure
groups.description: The Discovery tab is a multi-view panel (configure, history, report) for automated state exploration. In the configure view, users select an exploration strategy (smoke_test, exhaustive, regression, random_walk, targeted), configure advanced options (max states, state delay, screenshots, stop on failure), preview the exploration plan, and start an exploration run. The panel shows the config name and state/transition counts.

assertions.description: The discovery panel shows a 'State Explorer' heading in the configure view
A 'Strategy' label identifies the exploration strategy selector
Users can select an exploration strategy from a dropdown with options including Smoke Test, Exhaustive, Regression, Random Walk, and Targeted

target.label: Strategy selector with Smoke Test option

assertions.description: A 'Preview Plan' button generates and shows a preview of the exploration plan without running it
A 'Start Exploration' button begins the automated exploration run against the active config
An 'Advanced Options' toggle expands additional configuration fields for max states, state delay, screenshots, and stop-on-failure
A 'History' button navigates to the exploration history view showing past runs

groups.name: Discovery Tab: Advanced Options
groups.description: When the 'Advanced Options' toggle is expanded, it reveals configuration fields: Max states (number input, 0 = unlimited), State delay in ms (number input, default 500), Capture screenshots (checkbox, default on), Stop on first failure (checkbox, default off). These are shown in a left-bordered section.

assertions.description: A 'Max states (0 = unlimited)' label identifies the maximum states input
assertions.expected: Max states

assertions.description: A 'State delay (ms)' label identifies the delay between state exploration steps
assertions.expected: State delay

assertions.description: A 'Capture screenshots' checkbox allows toggling screenshot capture during exploration
A 'Stop on first failure' checkbox allows halting exploration when a failure is encountered

groups.name: Discovery Tab: Exploration History
groups.description: The history view shows a list of past exploration runs with config name, strategy, start timestamp, and summary. Each run has a 'View Report' link. A refresh button reloads the history, and a 'Clear runs older than 30 days' button purges old entries. When no runs exist, an empty state message is shown.

assertions.description: The history view shows an 'Exploration History' heading
When no exploration runs exist, the history shows 'No exploration runs yet' as an empty state
A 'Configure' back button returns to the configure view from the history view
A 'Clear runs older than 30 days' button purges stale exploration history entries
assertions.expected: Clear runs older than 30 days
preconditions: History view with at least one run

groups.name: Discovery Tab: Exploration Report
groups.description: The report view shows detailed results of a single exploration run: summary stats (states passed/visited, transitions passed/verified, duration, strategy), per-state results with status icons, per-transition results with from/to labels, and an optional summary text. A 'Back' button returns to the history view.

assertions.description: The report view shows an 'Exploration Report' heading
The report shows a 'States Passed' stat card with the count of passed vs visited states
The report shows a 'Transitions Passed' stat card with the count of passed vs verified transitions
The report shows a 'Duration' stat card with the total exploration time
A 'Back' button returns from the report view to the history view

groups.name: Live Test Tab: Main Controls
groups.description: The Live Test tab provides interactive state machine testing. It has three sections: Execute Transition (with a searchable transition list and quick-execute buttons), Navigate to State (dropdown + navigate button), and an Activity Log. The tab requires a running Python executor.

assertions.description: The Live Test panel shows a 'Live Test' heading
A note reminds users that the Live Test requires a running executor process
An 'Execute Transition' section label identifies the transition execution area
Users can filter the transition list with a 'Filter transitions...' search input
A 'Navigate to State' section label identifies the state navigation area
A 'Navigate' button triggers navigation to the selected state via the navigate_to_state IPC command

groups.name: Live Test: Transition List and Quick Execute
groups.description: The transition list shows each transition with name, from/to state labels, and a quick-execute play button. Clicking a row selects it; clicking the play icon immediately executes the transition. The selected transition shows an 'Execute: <name>' button with action count and cost info. Filtering by name or state names is supported.

assertions.description: Each transition in the list shows the transition name, from-state names (blue), a chevron arrow, and to-state names (green)
assertions.expected: Each transition row should display: transition name (truncated), from-states in blue text, a chevron arrow, and activate-states in green text. Each row should also have a play icon button for quick execution.
preconditions: A config is selected with transitions

assertions.description: Each transition row has a play icon button that immediately executes that transition via the execute_transition IPC command without requiring selection first
assertions.expected: Each transition row should have a small play (triangle) icon button on the right side that executes the transition when clicked. The button should be disabled during execution.
preconditions: A config is selected with transitions

assertions.description: When a transition is selected, an 'Execute: <name>' button appears below the list showing the action count and path cost
assertions.expected: After clicking a transition row, an 'Execute: <transition name>' button should appear below the list, alongside text showing 'N action(s) · cost: X.X'
preconditions: A config is selected with transitions

assertions.description: When no transitions exist or match the filter, the transition list shows an appropriate empty state message
assertions.expected: When the config has no transitions: 'No transitions'. When filter has no matches: 'No matching transitions'.

groups.name: Live Test: Activity Log
groups.description: The activity log shows timestamped entries for transitions executed, navigations performed, info messages, and errors. Each entry is color-coded by type (blue for transitions, cyan for navigate, gray for info, red for errors). Refresh and clear buttons are provided. When empty, a placeholder message is shown.

assertions.description: An 'Activity Log' section label identifies the log area
When no activity has occurred, the log shows an instructional empty state message
assertions.expected: No activity yet

assertions.description: A state selector dropdown with 'Select a state...' placeholder allows choosing a target state for navigation
Activity log entries are color-coded by type: blue for transition executions, cyan for navigations, gray for info, red for errors, with monospace timestamps
assertions.expected: After executing a transition or navigating, log entries should appear with: a monospace timestamp, color-coded message text (blue-400 for transitions, cyan-400 for navigate, text-secondary for info, red-400 for errors). Most recent entries appear at the top.
preconditions: At least one operation has been executed

groups.name: Error Display and Loading States
groups.description: The page displays errors from the useStateMachineConfig hook in a red banner at the bottom of the page. Import errors appear in the export tab. The Live Test panel has its own error banner. Loading states are indicated by Loader2 spinner icons throughout the page.

assertions.description: When the useStateMachineConfig hook encounters an error, a red error banner appears at the bottom of the page displaying the error message
assertions.expected: When an IPC command fails (e.g., sm_list_configs, sm_create_config), a red-tinted banner should appear at the bottom of the page with the error message text. The banner has bg-red-500/10 background and red-500/20 border styling.

assertions.description: During async operations (loading configs, creating states/transitions), a loading spinner is displayed in the header area
assertions.expected: A spinning Loader2 icon should appear in the header (ml-auto position) when isLoading is true, indicating an async operation is in progress
preconditions: An async operation is in progress

assertions.description: When a config import fails (invalid JSON or missing states/transitions fields), a red error message appears in the Export/Import tab
assertions.expected: After a failed import, a red error message should appear in the Export/Import tab showing the error reason (e.g., 'Invalid config format: missing states or transitions')

assertions.description: When a Live Test operation fails, a dedicated error banner appears in the Live Test panel with a dismiss button

target.label: Live Test error banner with dismiss

assertions.expected: When a transition execution or state navigation fails in the Live Test tab, a red error banner should appear showing the error message with a 'dismiss' underlined link to clear it
preconditions: A transition or navigation has failed
